findings.title: URL-triggered debug/E2E drivers wipe and overwrite player saves in production
findings.vulnerability_class: active debug code reachable via untrusted input; destructive storage action (CWE-489)
findings.threat_model: Attacker crafts a link to the deployed origin with ?autotest=1 or ?scenario=<any value>; any victim who opens it loses local save data (story save wiped by runAutotest; world save deleted/overwritten by runScenario) and the game auto-plays in their browser. No account, code execution, or exfiltration involved.
findings.description: Both drivers dispatch on mere query-param presence with no value check, no navigator.webdriver gate (that gate only skips the cinematic), no import.meta guard (none exists in src/), and no confirmation prompt. runAutotest calls wipeSave() as its first act; runScenario removes and rewrites the world-save key multiple times.
evidence: Source trace: Game.ts:468-480 dispatches on params.has(...) and dynamically imports autotest/scenario in the production bundle (no feature flags; deploy-pages.yml builds unflagged).
Seam-level dynamic proof (evidence/RESULTS-wipe-seam.txt): wipeSave() removes key first_slice_save_v1; a seeded day-4/$240 save becomes defaults (day=1, money=87).
Verifier A: confirmed; verified no confirm()/prompt() exists in src and that the webdriver gate does not cover these paths.
findings.impact: Loss of the victim's local game progress (story and/or world layer) plus an unwanted auto-play session. No confidentiality impact, no code execution, no persistent compromise.
findings.exploitability: Trivial attacker effort (one crafted link), one-click victim. Severity bounded by asset value: regenerable local game progress in a single-player game.

remediation.root_cause: Game.ts dispatched both debug drivers on mere URL-param presence (params.has(...)) with no authorization signal of any kind; autotest.ts:439 called wipeSave() (the player story save) as its first act; scenario.ts removed/rewrote the world-save key; production builds shipped both chunks and the dispatch, so one crafted link destroyed another person's save data.
remediation.design: One explicit development/production boundary (web-three/src/game/driverGate.ts) + a driver storage sandbox:
implementation: NEW web-three/src/game/driverGate.ts — the single decision point: authorizeDebugDrivers({devMode, handshake}) (pure, unit-tested), readDriverHandshake(sessionStorage) reading fs_driver_authorized==='1', enableDriverStorageSandbox() re-keying story+world persistence, isDriverAuthorizedNow() for defense-in-depth entry checks. The module header IS the documentation of the boundary; there is no hidden query parameter.

web-three/src/core/Save.ts — driver sandbox keys: DRIVER_SAVE_KEY ('first_slice_save_v1_driver'), setStorySaveKeyOverride(), activeSaveKey(); loadSave/writeSave/wipeSave ride the ACTIVE key. Outside an authorized session the behavior is byte-identical to before.
web-three/src/sim/state.ts — DRIVER_WORLD_SAVE_KEY ('first_slice_world_v1_driver'), setWorldSaveKeyOverride(), activeWorldSaveKey(); worldRuntime storage routes through it.

web-three/src/game/Game.ts — the authorization is decided FIRST in the constructor (before any storage read); an authorized session enables the sandbox and announces it in the console; both URL dispatches now require driverAuth.allowed, and a denied request is honestly logged ('[driver] ?autotest ignored — debug drivers are gated in production builds').

web-three/src/game/autotest.ts + scenario.ts — defense in depth: both drivers re-check isDriverAuthorizedNow() at entry and refuse otherwise; autotest's wipeSave() comment documents the sandbox routing.
web-three/src/game/worldRuntime.ts — all three storage touchpoints (constructor read, flushWorldSave, reloadFromSave) plus debug().saveKey route through activeWorldSaveKey().

scripts/e2e.mjs + scripts/probe-world-sim.mjs — the harnesses authorize themselves via page.addInitScript(() => sessionStorage.setItem('fs_driver_authorized','1')) BEFORE any page script runs — the documented non-URL path; the fleet keeps working against real built production output.
guarantees: Production + URL alone (any params): drivers never start; the boundary says so in the console; no sandbox key is created.

An authorized driver session is STORAGE-SANDBOXED: every story read/write/wipe rides first_slice_save_v1_driver and every world read/write rides first_slice_world_v1_driver — a real player save is unreachable by construction, not by discipline.
The wardrobe 'start over' reset (Game.ts beginNewGameAs) is a player-confirmed UI action and is intentionally NOT part of the URL surface; it is unchanged.
Normal gameplay URL behavior (?starter, ?film, ?pickcard, ?worldclock, ?fx) is unchanged; the boot law, save law, schema, and calendar epoch are untouched.
regression_tests: tests/driver-gate.test.ts (14 cases): the authorization matrix (dev/handshake/denied), handshake = sessionStorage never URL, storage-refusing browser denies, sandbox re-keys both layers, wipeSave() in a driver session hits only the driver key, a full driver write/read/wipe cycle never touches the player key, the schema is unchanged by the sandbox.

scripts/probe-security-r1.mjs (31 checks, real dist/): P1 ?autotest=1 → driver never starts, seeded day-4/$240 story save intact; P2/P2b/P3/P4 ?scenario=x / schedules / both / hostile → world save byte-identical, no driver, no page errors; N1 plain load unchanged (bootedFromDay 4); D1 authorized ?autotest=1 → driver starts AND boots from the driver key (bootedFromDay=1 with a day-4 player save present), player save intact; D2 authorized ?scenario=schedules → scenario streams on the driver world key, real world save byte-identical.
scripts/e2e.mjs (4-day story E2E against dist/) — updated for the handshake; full proof the authorized fleet path works.
scripts/probe-world-sim.mjs — updated for the handshake; the 15-step scenario battery on the sandboxed world key.

remediation.residual_risk: None known for the URL→destruction path. The handshake (sessionStorage) can be set by anyone with devtools access to their OWN browser — an explicit local developer action, equivalent to typing JavaScript in the console; it cannot be triggered remotely and destroys only sandbox keys. The driver chunks still ship in the production bundle (dynamically imported only behind the gate); a future hardening could exclude them at build time if the fleet ever moves off built-output testing.

findings.title: World-save parser contradicts its documented degrade law: shape-broken sections throw; only the boot-seam catch prevents a crash
findings.vulnerability_class: improper validation on deserialization; contract violation (CWE-502 family)
findings.threat_model: No remote vector. Requires a JSON-valid but shape-broken world save in the victim's localStorage (hand-editing, buggy third-party save tool, storage corruption preserving JSON validity). The browser itself always writes typed documents.
findings.description: parseWorldSave validates only magic/version/worldId then casts to WorldSaveDocument unchecked; hydrate dereferences doc.clock.day, doc.player.moneyCents, doc.relationships.map, doc.ledger.txns, doc.flags without validation. The module header promises 'anything missing/invalid/corrupt degrades to a fresh, valid world... never a crash'; the implementation throws, and survives only because bootWorldBrain catches.
evidence: Harness battery on production modules (evidence/RESULTS-save-parsers.txt, B2-B7, B13): missing ledger/clock/player, relationships:5, ledger.txns:5, flags:[1,2,3], junk npcs all throw TypeError.
Validated refusals still work (B8-B10: wrong magic, version 99, foreign worldId -> fresh).
Verifier A: the only two callers of parseWorldSave sit inside the bootWorldBrain try/catch; main.ts adds an outer net.
findings.impact: Unexpected silent world-layer resets for a user with a damaged world save; the corrupt document is not quarantined and the reset repeats until the next flush overwrites it. No crash, no code execution, no cross-principal effect.
findings.exploitability: Not remotely exploitable; realistic only via local tampering/corruption. Architectural weight: the central persistence law currently hangs on one catch block in a different module.

remediation.root_cause: parseWorldSave (sim/state.ts) validated only magic/version/worldId and then blind-cast the document into hydrate(), which dereferenced doc.clock.day, doc.relationships.map, doc.ledger.txns, doc.flags, and entity rows unchecked — shape-broken-but-JSON-valid documents threw; the documented 'corrupt save is a fresh start, never a crash' law held only because bootWorldBrain (sim/runtime.ts) happened to catch, two files away. The refused document also stayed on the active key, so the reset repeated on every boot until an autosave healed it.
remediation.design: Full pre-hydration validation with whitelist reconstruction (all-or-nothing), a guarded hydrate as a second net, an integrity gate, and quarantine-not-destroy recovery:
implementation: web-three/src/sim/state.ts — NEW validation battery (~470 lines): every section (seed, clock, player, npcs, relationships, businesses, ledger.txns+seq, flags, chapter.rails, missable, consequences, events, environment) is type-checked, range-checked (MAX_MONEY_CENTS=100_000_000; day 1..36500 = the project's own clampCalendarDay bound; minute 0..1439; tick bounds; warmth -100..100; trust 0..100; ledger flow laws mirrored from sim/economy post()), id-validated against the sim-id/registry-id grammars (sim/ids.ts, isAccount), reference-validated (relationships→npcs, businesses→npcs, flows→accounts), array-bound-checked (npcs ≤10k, txns ≤50k, flags ≤1k...), duplicate-checked (npc/rel/txn ids), and REBUILT through a strict whitelist — unknown properties are DROPPED (the save.gd forward-compat law) and __proto__/constructor/prototype keys cannot survive reconstruction. Any failure → the whole document is refused: fresh world + one bounded diagnostic note ('world save rejected: <section>: <why> → fresh world') — no raw values echoed, no megabytes of narration.

parseWorldSave — new pipeline: magic/version/worldId (unchanged) → validateWorldSaveDocument → hydrate inside try/catch (second net: the module's contract no longer depends on any caller) → auditWorld gate: a post-hydration integrity failure (event order, dangling refs, ledger mismatch) REFUSES the document instead of silently accepting it.

web-three/src/game/worldRuntime.ts — quarantine: constructor + reloadFromSave move a REFUSED document (raw non-empty + source 'fresh') to first_slice_world_v1_quarantine (preserved, not destroyed) and clear the active key — the refusal happens once per document instead of once per boot, and the player continues on a fresh world. The story save rides a different key and is structurally untouched (bootWorldBrain is pure: zero storage writes).
web-three/src/sim/runtime.ts — bootWorldBrain's catch remains as the outer net (unchanged contract: fresh + note).
compatibility: Valid saves restore exactly: the 840-test baseline suite (incl. the sim-state round-trip and 'broken money reported, not hidden' genesis-clamp case) passes UNCHANGED at 840/840 before the new batteries were added.
Unknown trailing fields are dropped, not rejected (forward compatibility, mirroring core/Save.ts's reader-names-its-fields law).
No schema change: the document written by snapshotWorld() parses exactly as before; the parser only became stricter about what it accepts.

The FS-AUDIT-003 reproduction (player.moneyCents=1e12) now lands on the new money-ceiling rejection (bounded at $1M) — the structural finding (self-consistent doc-derived economics) remains open for the WP-4 re-audit as scheduled.
regression_tests: tests/world-save-validation.test.ts (33 cases): the audit B-battery re-ported (missing/null ledger, clock, player, relationships, npcs, flags; wrong primitives; invalid txn arrays incl. self-transfer and world-account flow laws; day 0/1e15; minute 1440; calendarDay overflow; warmth/trust ranges; junk npc rows; duplicate ids; rails junk; flag tuples; environment values; 1e12/1e15 money; seed overflow; JSON 1e999) + prototype-pollution payloads (__proto__ in doc, rails, environment; constructor keys; arrays-for-objects) + resource bounds (10,001 npcs / 50,001 txns refused at the bound) + integrity-gate cases (unordered events, double-listed relationship, non-item inventory id) + valid-save round-trips (clock/warmth/flags/ledger/npcs exact; unknown fields dropped; restored world audits clean) + a hostile parse-never-throws corpus + bootWorldBrain recovery (fresh brain + reference cast + playable clock advance) + storage-isolation proof (a recording storage stub: bootWorldBrain performs ZERO storage writes; the story save is byte-identical).

scripts/probe-security-r2.mjs (166 checks, real dist/): 21 corruption classes through the production recovery seam (reloadFromSave) — each: fresh world, named note, story save intact, refused doc quarantined, world playable; C14 valid doc restores; C15 post-quarantine boot is clean (loop ended); B1/B2 cold-boot constructor-path proofs.
remediation.verification_evidence: docs/security-audit/evidence/RESULTS-probe-security-r2.txt (166/166), RESULTS-vitest-r1-r2.txt (892/892 incl. world-save-validation.test.ts), RESULTS-save-parsers.txt (original audit battery, preserved)

follow_up.trigger: independent verifier finding N-1 (2026-11-07), fixed in the same branch
follow_up.N-1_ledger_replay_gate: the verifier demonstrated a shape-valid doc whose ledger history could not be replayed (overdraft at rehydration) restoring SILENTLY with divergent business balances — hydrate's post() rejections (world.ledger.issues) were never consulted. The parse-time integrity gate now refuses on world.ledger.issues.length > 0 (notes carry the bounded OVERDRAFT/policy details), and a regression test reproduces the verifier's exact attack (biz→npc→biz overdraft loop → fresh world + note). For documents the live game writes, replay replicates the original policy-checked sequence exactly, so the new refusal cannot fire on a valid save.
follow_up.N-5_consistency_blemishes: verifier-observed silent-restore blemishes (dangling npc→rel reference, same-pair double rel edges, ghost event npcIds) recorded as INFORMATIONAL — no crash path; candidates for the next hardening pass

remediation.residual_risk: The genesis-clamp recovery (doc balances inconsistent with their own txns in a way the clamp absorbs) still restores with a loud note and preserved balances — a documented, bounded recovery, not a silent acceptance; with the N-1 gate, everything the replay cannot reproduce is refused. FS-AUDIT-003's structural economics trust gap (doc-derived genesis) is intentionally out of scope here and remains gated on the WP-4 re-audit (the verifier confirmed N-1 belongs to the same trust family).
remediation.independent_reviewer_verdict: HOLDS — survived an adversarial re-verification by a separate agent (2026-11-07). The verifier ran 25+ hostile documents through the real parseWorldSave (all 12 sections missing/null, wrong primitives, 1e12/1e15 numerics, __proto__/constructor keys, arrays-for-objects, resource bounds, duplicates, dangling refs): zero throws, zero partial hydrations, zero malformed docs restored; the 840-test baseline passes unchanged (suite now 892/892); recovery provably performs zero storage writes and never touches the story save; quarantine refusal conditions verified exact. The verifier's strongest attack (N-1: hydrate-time post() rejections silently swallowed) was FIXED in the same branch — the integrity gate now refuses any document whose ledger history cannot be replayed — and is pinned by a regression test reproducing the exact attack. Residual consistency blemishes (N-5) are recorded as informational; the structural economics gap remains FS-AUDIT-003 / WP-4 as scheduled.

findings.title: World restore re-derives economic truth from the save document; integrity audit is blind to tampered balances
findings.vulnerability_class: second-order trust gap: untrusted persisted state treated as economic truth, masked by a self-referential integrity check
findings.threat_model: Attacker = the local player (self-impact; ordinary client-side cheating). Becomes a real trust-boundary failure only if world state feeds a shared/server-side consumer (the roadmap's D-3 money bridge).
findings.description: hydrate() re-derives ledger genesis from the document's final balances, so hand-edited player.moneyCents is self-consistent by construction; auditWorld then compares two doc-derived values and returns zero issues. Harness case B11: moneyCents=1e12 restores as source='restored' with zero notes.
evidence: Verifier A confirmed the D-3 money bridge is open work (AGENTS.md:11, docs/architecture/world-contract/17-implementation-roadmap.md, docs/production/NEXT-PHASE-EXECUTION-PLAN.md).
findings.impact: Self-impact cheating today. Forward risk: a money-printing primitive with a blind audit if the D-3 bridge (or any shared/online feature) consumes world state.
findings.remediation: When the money bridge lands: treat ledger transactions (not final balances) as trusted input, recompute balances, and plausibility-clamp restored economics with a note; reject/flag worlds failing re-simulation.
findings.regression_test: When the bridge lands: a restored world with doc money inconsistent with re-simulated transactions must be flagged/rejected.

findings.title: GameClock accepts unbounded day; calendarOf() is linear in day - latent multi-hour loop with no shipped consumer
findings.vulnerability_class: unbounded loop over attacker-influenced numeric input (CWE-400 family) - currently unreachable
findings.threat_model: Requires a world save with clock.day=1e15 (local tampering; accepted, proven) AND a consumer reading .date/.season on the world clock. No such consumer exists today (exhaustive grep, verifier-confirmed).
findings.description: Measured: day=1e7 -> 27,398 iterations in 0.69ms (linear). day=1e15 projects ~2.7e12 iterations (multi-hour hang). Not executed (bounded-test rule). weekdayOf is O(1); advanceReal is capped at 1440 ticks/call; story-side calendar values are clamped to 36500.
evidence: Verifier B consumer census: no .date/.season reader on any clock.
findings.impact: None today; one future consumer away from a persistent tab freeze fed by a hand-edited save.
findings.exploitability: Not reachable in the shipped build.
findings.remediation: Clamp day in the GameClock constructor (Math.min(36500, ...)) mirroring clampCalendarDay.
findings.regression_test: new GameClock({day: 1e15}).day === 36500; calendarOf bounded after clamp.

reconciliation.source_change_since_baseline: sim/clock.ts byte-identical (git diff = 0). NEW: sim/epochMap.ts (WP-2v) imports calendarOf/weekdayOf and is the first new production consumer of calendar math since the audit.
reconciliation.reachability_change: none — examined line by line: epochMap calls calendarOf only with the constant 1 (:183) and loop day <= 1460 (:210-212); every public mapping function routes through assertDay() (:69-76) which throws on non-integer, <1, or >36500; epochAgreement is boot/audit-time ('never per frame', :167) and its walk is bounded. No unbounded production consumer of GameClock day/.date/.season exists at 62a6244. The latent hazard (GameClock constructor unclamped, clock.ts:148) is byte-identical.
reconciliation.dynamic_evidence_at_current: R2 battery R4.1/R4.2/R4.3/R4.4: world-save clock.day=1e15 accepted, new GameClock({day:1e15}).day=1e15 (unclamped), calendarOf(1e7) 0.43ms (linear), weekday O(1); R5.1-R5.11: epochMap strict front door throws on 0/NaN/1.5/36501/1e15, simTickOfStoryDay(1)=460, epochAgreement().agreed=true, tolerant read clamps (evidence/RESULTS-reconciliation-62a6244.txt)
reconciliation.watch_item: epochMap exports datelineOfSimDay/datelineOfStoryDay for the roadmap's WP-6 (HUD/diary datelines). WP-6 is the exact 'future consumer' this finding warned about — routing through epochMap is safe (assertDay bounds to 36500, ~1ms), but a WP-6 surface that reads GameClock day directly (bypassing the mapping) would reactivate the latent hang. R4 (clamp GameClock) remains the durable fix.

remediation_qa_full_spectrum.fix: GameClock carries the day trust boundary itself: the constructor clamps day to [1,36500] and advance pins at the ceiling (the final day still flows; no day may open past 36500). calendarOf can never be handed an unbounded day again — the latent tab-freeze class is dead at the source. WP-6's HUD dateline was verified already routed through epochMap's bounded mapping.

findings.threat_model: Requires hand-edited first_slice_album; only writers are canvas toDataURL raster captures. SVG via executes no script and loads no external resources (SVG-as-image mode).
findings.description: isDataImage accepts any data:image/ prefix; thumbs reach only img.src. Re-share/download paths treat thumbs as opaque bytes. javascript: URIs and oversized values are rejected.
evidence: Verifier B corrected one line reference and confirmed all sinks.
